extracted.intended_audience: H-1B petitioners/registrants, employers, and immigration attorneys/stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Rules governing how registrants/petitioners must select, document, and justify OEWS wage levels (and related identifiers, SOC codes, locations) for H-1B registrations and subsequent petitions, along with integrity and enforcement measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of the basis of the wage level selected on the registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners must submit evidence of the basis of the wage level selected on the registration as of the date that the registration underlying the petition was submitted (new 8 CFR 214.2(h)(8)(iii)(D)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence could include, but is not limited to, a printout from the DOL OFLC Wage Search website for the beneficiary’s SOC code and area(s) of intended employment as of the date of registration. Where an alternate wage source is used, submit evidence appropriate to that source (e.g., private wage survey, collective bargaining agreement). Petitioners may also wish to submit an explanation of any relevant changes in OEWS wage data with the petition. If registration is suspended, evidence should reflect the date of petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage level must reflect OEWS data as of registration date (or petition date if suspended)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OEWS wage level selected must reflect the corresponding OEWS wage level as of the date that the registration underlying the petition was submitted; however, if the registration process is suspended, the OEWS wage level selected must reflect the corresponding OEWS wage level as of the date that the petition is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if OEWS wage data changes between registration and petition filing, the Form I-129 box should reflect information current at time of registration (or petition if registration suspended). Example: if proffered wage corresponded to level IV at registration but OEWS later corresponds to level III, the registrant should still select level IV on Form I-129 if registration-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select the highest OEWS wage level the proffered wage equals or exceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: On the registration (or petition, if registration suspended), the registrant must select the highest OEWS wage level that the beneficiary’s proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC code in the area(s) of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This selection is used for weighting/selection. It is distinct from the LCA wage-level selection (see separate criterion). Registrants should follow the form instructions (Form I-129, Section 3, question 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish registration wage level from LCA wage-level obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The wage level selected on the LCA may differ from the appropriate wage level selected on the registration because the rule allows registrants to choose the highest OEWS wage level that the proffered wage equals or exceeds for registration purposes, while the LCA process is governed by DOL prevailing-wage and actual-wage requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must follow DOL instructions for the LCA, which requires attesting that H-1B nonimmigrants will be paid either the actual wage or the prevailing wage (whichever is greater). The registration selection is a separate weighting input and need not mirror the LCA if facts differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use OEWS as the authoritative source for weighting registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will use OEWS prevailing wage levels to rank and select registrations (or petitions) by wage level because OEWS is the most comprehensive and objective publicly available source for comparing wages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OEWS produces employment and wage estimates annually for approximately 830 occupations and is accessible via DOL's FLAG system. Alternative sources may lack public availability or standard four-level structures, so OEWS is the baseline for selection weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of alternative/non-OEWS prevailing wage sources
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant relies on a prevailing wage that is not based on the OEWS survey and the proffered wage is less than the corresponding level I OEWS wage, the registrant should select the 'wage level I' box on the registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners may continue to use private wage surveys, CBAs, SCA determinations, or other legitimate sources to establish they will pay the required wage, but DHS will generally group non-OEWS-based registrations with Level I for selection weighting. Petitioners relying on non-OEWS sources may choose to increase proffered wages to improve selection odds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow DOL Prevailing Wage Determination guidance if no current OEWS data
rubrics_metrics.description: In the limited instance where there is no current OEWS prevailing wage information for the proffered position, the registrant must follow DOL guidance on prevailing wage determinations (PWDs) to determine which OEWS wage level to select.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM cited DOL ETA Prevailing Wage Determination Policy Guidance: Nonagricultural Immigration Programs (Nov. 2009) as the guidance to apply; registrants should use the version of DOL guidance in effect at the time, including any future updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use lowest corresponding OEWS wage level for multi-location or multi-position roles
rubrics_metrics.description: If the beneficiary will work in multiple locations, or in multiple positions (e.g., agent placements), the petitioner must select the lowest corresponding OEWS wage level that the beneficiary’s proffered wage will equal or exceed across those locations/positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must submit evidence supporting the selected basis (e.g., separate DOL OFLC Wage Search printouts for each location and each position). USCIS will consider all submitted evidence plus registration/LCA/petition information to determine if the lowest corresponding level was selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign beneficiary to the lowest OEWS wage level among all registrations filed on their behalf
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple employers register or petition on behalf of the same individual at various corresponding wage levels, DHS will assign the beneficiary to the lowest OEWS wage level among all registrations for weighted selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach is intended to reduce incentives for gaming (e.g., frivolous high-wage registrations). Employers/registrants are expected to communicate with beneficiaries about other registrations submitted on their behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification that registration represents a bona fide job offer (penalty of perjury)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the registration form, the registrant must certify under penalty of perjury that the registration represents a bona fide job offer and that the organization(s) intends to file an H-1B petition on behalf of the beneficiary if selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation is not required at registration because registrations are not adjudicated, but false certifications may prompt USCIS investigations. If a certification is found untrue, USCIS can find the registration not properly submitted, making the prospective petitioner ineligible to file a petition based on that registration (see new 8 CFR 214.2(h)(10)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary identification requirements and passport/travel-document evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must provide the beneficiary’s passport or travel document information at registration and petitioners are required to submit evidence of the passport/travel document used at registration when filing the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS does not require a scanned passport at registration, but the petition must be supported by the same identifying information. If passport numbers do not match, USCIS may deny or revoke the petition. USCIS may also deny or revoke for inaccurate, fraudulent, or materially misrepresentative statements and may refer cases for law enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency requirement between registration and subsequent petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The H-1B petition filed after registration selection must contain and be supported by the same position information and contain a proffered wage that equals or exceeds the prevailing wage for the corresponding OEWS wage level selected in the registration for the SOC code and area(s) of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS finalized integrity measures requiring petitions to be consistent with registration information; USCIS may deny subsequent new or amended petitions in certain circumstances suggesting attempts to unfairly increase selection odds (new 8 CFR 214.2(h)(8)(iii)(D)(1) and 8 CFR 214.2(h)(10)(iii)). These measures complement existing integrity provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS investigative and enforcement authority for false/misleading registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may investigate certifications made during registration, examine evidence of collusion and patterns of non-filing, and make findings of fraud or willful material misrepresentation where supported by the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If USCIS finds a certification was not true and correct, it may find the registration improperly submitted, render the prospective petitioner ineligible to file, deny or revoke petitions, and refer individuals or entities to appropriate Federal law enforcement agencies for investigation and further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: SOC code selection requirement and reliance on SOC for wage-level determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must select the appropriate SOC code when submitting an LCA and filing an H-1B petition, and DHS will rely on the SOC code (as used in the LCA/petition) to determine the corresponding OEWS wage level for registration weighting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS recognizes SOC codes are broad and may not capture nuanced differences across roles, but finds no viable alternative for classifying occupations for this rule. Employers should select SOC codes consistent with LCA/petition practice and offer commensurate wages reflective of skill/experience differences.
